cases.purpose: Look up the nlctrl controller by numeric ID in hexadecimal (0x10), decimal (16) and octal (020, strtoul base 0) and show that each prints the same nlctrl record as a lookup by name: the kernel ID, version, header size, max attribs, operations with capability flags and multicast groups.
cases.oracle: Independent kernel oracle: the helper's own NETLINK_GENERIC client (hand-encoded request builder, attribute parser including the nested operation and multicast-group arrays, several messages per buffer, several buffers per dump, NLMSG_DONE/NLMSG_ERROR/ACK handling, sequence and port matching) is first calibrated on hand-encoded vectors and then on the real guest kernel (by name, by id, dump, two interleaved requests, NLM_F_ACK, ENOENT); it is the only source of family IDs, versions, header sizes, operations, capability flags, multicast groups and errno values, so no expected value comes from candidate output. The text layout is the documented print contract of loadables/genl.c (bgenl_print_caps, bgenl_print_ops, bgenl_print_groups, bgenl_print_family_cb). The guest iproute2 genl is run on the same table as a gating control (name, id, version, header size and max attribs must agree with the raw oracle), so a disagreement is invalid evidence (a setup error), never a candidate result. The nlctrl record (id 0x10, discovered from the raw dump) is the expected content.
cases.comparison: semantic=yes means the stdout of each lookup, read by a tolerant parser, equals the oracle nlctrl record; same-as-name=yes means each id lookup is byte-identical to "ctrl get name nlctrl" from the same run; status is 0 with empty stderr. The same argv also runs through the guest iproute2 genl; its raw output and a structural comparison are saved in observations.jsonl and not asserted (byte parity with iproute2 is not part of this requirement; both raw outputs are kept so it can be examined offline). Every key is evaluated for every vector (no early exit). Retained in the case tree: the candidate's raw stdout, stderr and status for each vector (observations.jsonl), the raw oracle netlink transcripts (oracle-*transcript.jsonl), the iproute2 raw outputs (also in observations.jsonl); the setup control report is the stdout of the setup step.

cases.purpose: Invalid family IDs (non-numeric, above 0xffff, trailing junk) are rejected with "invalid family id" and the builtin usage status before any NETLINK socket is created; the boundary 0xffff and a valid ID show that the observer sees a netlink socket when one is opened.
cases.oracle: Usage status and diagnostic framing are learned from the reference bash 5.3.15 (a builtin usage error from "cd -z" shows the exact "NAME: line N: " prefix and status 2); the message text is the source contract of loadables/genl.c (builtin_error then EX_USAGE). Netlink I/O is observed with the pinned seccomp-notify helper system-sequence.py, which counts socket() calls after a captured stdout marker; setup calibrates it against children that create one netlink socket after the marker, none, and one before it. The raw kernel oracle confirms that 0xffff, the largest accepted 16-bit ID, is a valid unknown ID (ENOENT), so rejection at 0x10000 is the validation boundary.

Controls: a valid ID 16 and the boundary 0xffff each open exactly one netlink socket, and 0xffff produces no invalid-id diagnostic. Every key is evaluated for every vector (no early exit). cases.oracle: Independent kernel oracle: the helper's own NETLINK_GENERIC client (hand-encoded request builder, attribute parser including the nested operation and multicast-group arrays, several messages per buffer, several buffers per dump, NLMSG_DONE/NLMSG_ERROR/ACK handling, sequence and port matching) is first calibrated on hand-encoded vectors and then on the real guest kernel (by name, by id, dump, two interleaved requests, NLM_F_ACK, ENOENT); it is the only source of family IDs, versions, header sizes, operations, capability flags, multicast groups and errno values, so no expected value comes from candidate output. The text layout is the documented print contract of loadables/genl.c (bgenl_print_caps, bgenl_print_ops, bgenl_print_groups, bgenl_print_family_cb). The guest iproute2 genl is run on the same table as a gating control (name, id, version, header size and max attribs must agree with the raw oracle), so a disagreement is invalid evidence (a setup error), never a candidate result. Setup requires the guest table to contain operations with each of the four capability bits, so every word assertion is non-vacuous, and records how many operations carry none of the four bits. The word "none" (an operation with no flag word) stays an explicit gap: a generic-netlink operation must have a doit or dumpit handler, from which the kernel derives the DO/DUMP capability bit, so the real controller never reports such an operation (the setup count is the evidence), and no unprivileged synthetic controller exists for this loadable.

cases.purpose: The dump spans several receive buffers and ends with NLMSG_DONE; the candidate consumes all of it.
cases.oracle: Independent kernel oracle: the helper's own NETLINK_GENERIC client (hand-encoded request builder, attribute parser including the nested operation and multicast-group arrays, several messages per buffer, several buffers per dump, NLMSG_DONE/NLMSG_ERROR/ACK handling, sequence and port matching) is first calibrated on hand-encoded vectors and then on the real guest kernel (by name, by id, dump, two interleaved requests, NLM_F_ACK, ENOENT); it is the only source of family IDs, versions, header sizes, operations, capability flags, multicast groups and errno values, so no expected value comes from candidate output. Netlink I/O is observed with the pinned seccomp-notify helper system-sequence.py, which counts socket() calls after a captured stdout marker; setup calibrates it against children that create one netlink socket after the marker, none, and one before it. It also counts recvmsg() calls, calibrated against a child that performs a raw dump and reports its own recvmsg count. Setup requires the oracle's own dump to need at least two receive buffers that carry records, every record to carry NLM_F_MULTI and the dump to end with NLMSG_DONE; the same is re-checked before the run. If the guest family table fits in one buffer the control fails and the obligation stays open as a facility gap.
